newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends weak but losses limited.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends weak but losses limited.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mostly lower, although losses were limited by ongoing concern about spring wheat planting delays due to expected flooding in the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.

On a day that saw contracts in other U.S. wheat futures markets lose as much as 9-1/2 cents per bushel, MGE spring wheat settled steady to only 2-3/4 cents lower, with May down two cents at $4.00-3/4. New crop September closed down 1-1/2 cents at $3.84-1/4.
"Deferreds were real strong -- nobody wants to sell them," a trader said.

Traders said Linnco Futures bought around one million Sept bushels. In options trade, Atwood/Peavey bought at least 100 of the May $4.00 calls at 12-1/2 cents per bushel. Traders speculated this was tied to flour mill business.
MGE barley futures did not trade.
